production.note: US model years, from Kelley Blue Book (a database): its Revuelto page lists 2026, 2025 and 2024 in the year selector. Still on sale. Carscoops (carscoops-revuelto) reports the reveal on 29 March 2023.

configuration.note: Lamborghini: "a new V12 engine, three electric motors and a dual-clutch e-gearbox"; Evo panel: "Engine | 6.5-litre V12 & three electric motors".

aspiration.note: Top Gear: "The headline figures for this nat asp monster are 814bhp at 9,250rpm".

fuel.note: Carscoops: "3.8 kWh battery charges in 30 minutes using a 7 kW supply"; Top Gear (topgear-revuelto): "There's a 3.8kWh battery pack".

drivetrain.note: Carscoops: "two 148 hp (150 PS) units in the nose driving the front wheels" with the V12 and a third motor driving the rear.

transmission.note: Evo: "an eight-speed DCT gearbox"; Carscoops: "eight-speed dual-clutch transmission".

powerHp.note: Combined system output. Quote (Lamborghini model page): "Max power (combined ICE+EE): 1015 CV/ 747 kW". 1,015 CV x 0.98632 = 1,001 hp. Evo panel (evo-revuelto): "Power | 1001bhp"; Carscoops (carscoops-revuelto): "1,001 hp (1,015 PS)"; KBB: "Horsepower-Combined | 1001 @ 9250 RPM". V12 alone: "814 hp (825 PS)" (Carscoops). No separate US SAE rating was found, so powerStandard is DIN PS.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (guide step 4). Quote (Evo spec panel, review by Richard Meaden, Jethro Bovingdon and Yousuf Ashraf): "Weight | 1772kg (dry)". 1,772 x 2.20462 = 3,907 lb. Carscoops (carscoops-revuelto): "dry weight of 3,907 lbs (1,772 kg)"; Top Gear (topgear-revuelto): "Lamborghini claims a dry weight of 1,772kg, which means over 1,900kg with fluids." No curb weight for the standard car (steps 1 and 2) and no optioned-car curb weight (step 3) was found from Lamborghini or a major magazine; Lamborghini's model page gives no weight. No opened page says whether the dry figure assumes options.
